Built the family×prime incidence matrix (families = (★) levels C=1..40, A[C,p]=1 iff 4Cp+1 has a divisor ≡ −1 (4C); 3000 primes p ≡ 1 (4) after 10⁶; density 0.133) and compared singular values with curveball degree-preserving shuffles. Against the global null the 2nd/3rd singular values are in excess (29.85, 27.56 vs 27.14, 26.38; z = 13.5, 8.7), but a null that shuffles only within columns of equal p mod 840 (moves ~55–59% of the ones) reproduces the whole spectrum (|z| ≤ 1.2; mod 9240 likewise). So all collective structure visible spectrally is the residue class of p (the local-density effect of RESIDUE_HARDNESS.md), with no extra arithmetic coupling between levels — a clean but modest calibration of the independent-incidence/lottery model.

summary: BLINDNESS CAVEAT: a repo grep for 'Sidorenko' accidentally displayed Haiku's one-line Pass-1 verdict for this item (ES_CONNECTIONS_TODO.md) before my attempt. Proof attempt with concrete hosts: (i) the shift–divisor graph u ~ m iff m | p+u (≈U log p edges, density forced) — certificates are coloured EDGES (m ≡ −1 mod 4u), and every 2-path/4-cycle u–m–u′ forces m | u−u′, i.e. m ≤ U: pattern counts live only on small moduli (privacy of large primes, SS8 Lemma 2.3), congruence data blind at T1; (ii) the hyperbola xy ≡ 1 (4p) (≍p edges, Weil-quasirandom) — a certificate is an edge with a height-dependent congruence (the tied modulus, FRONTIER §3), again not a pattern. General screen (elementary): Blakley–Roy/Cauchy–Schwarz gives ≥ n·d̄(d̄−1) non-degenerate 2-paths, so a host with p^{Ω(1)} vertices and forced density yields p^{Ω(1)} copies vs ≍log²p certificates (B3: fibres ≥ p^{Ω(1)}), and if the density forcing is uniform in n it also holds at odd squares, contradicting T1 unless the host's edges are themselves T1-sensitive (i.e. B2 events). The thick-extremal analogue (Paley/Hoffman forcing needs sets ≥ √p; word sets are polylog) is already in BRAINSTORM/z52_deep_thin_pointwise_opus.md §2.4.

summary: Did the step: for N = 12p+1 (level t=12), D⁻(N) = #{d | N : d ≡ −1 (12)} = (τ − σ_{χ−4} − σ_{χ−3} + σ_{χ12})(N)/4 matches direct enumeration at all 9590 primes < 10⁵ (0 mismatches). Since (ℤ/12)^× is elementary-2 every character is a genus character, so level 12 is pure genus: D⁻(12p+1)=0 at 6411/9590 primes, exactly when one odd character is trivial on all prime factors — 2687 with all factors ≡ 1 (12), 2156 with only χ_{−4} trivial (the 'other genus character', not tied to p), 1568 with only χ_{−3} trivial (χ_{−3}(ℓ) = (p/ℓ)-type, the BM/Lemma-CT layer). This is FRONTIER §2.1 (genus split), §2.3 (Thm K: odd-character component = theta quotient) and §7.3 (n = 7 at t = 12 obstructed by another genus character); the expansion itself is textbook orthogonality.

Ran the step on 150 Mordell-hard primes after 10⁷, all prime e ≡ 3 (4) ≤ 200, both types (7200 e-slices; Q = Σ_e(N) per LONGSHOT_PIGEONHOLE Lemma 1.1). Raw: slices with a prime factor of N that is a primitive root mod e succeed 51.4% vs 7.8% without — but this is entirely the quadratic layer: with no QNR factor the success rate is exactly 0 (−1 is a QNR mod e; Lemma 1.2/T1 parity), and among slices that have a QNR factor the primitive-root lift is 51.4% vs 45.6%, and vanishes or reverses when also stratified by ω(N) (e.g. ω=3: 35.6% vs 39.8%; ω=4: 61.7% vs 58.1%). So Artin/primitive-root abundance carries no information about the class beyond its quadratic character (as CLASS_FORCING's 'parity, never class' predicts); the exponent-realisation issue (ℓ^{(e−1)/2} | N) makes a primitive root alone almost never produce −1.

Computed the Ramanujan regrouping R(n) = Σ_d S_d(n), S_d = Σ_{(u,C): d|m} c_d(n+u)/m (exact; Hölder formula), binned in d, at three odd squares ≈10⁵ (301², 315², 317²), two (★)-failure primes (83449, 102001) and three control primes (R = 24–38). The d=1 main term is ≈16.2 (≈ log²n/8) everywhere; at squares and failure primes the cancellation is spread over all scales with no T1-specific level — e.g. 315²: d∈[2,10] −9.5, d>10⁴ −4.0; 317²: d∈[2,100] +1.5, d∈[101,10⁴] −10.2, d>10⁴ −7.6 — and squares look like (★)-failure primes (both have ≈4–8 of the 16 cancelled only by d > 10⁴, i.e. d ≍ m). So the additive (Ramanujan/Fourier) expansion does not localise T1: T1 is a multiplicative quadratic-character effect (χ_{−4uB}) that is smeared across every d up to the tied modulus, and no truncation in d approximates R.
